page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a high-capacity server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 144 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 540 GB of RAM, providing a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 156268.58 and a Passmark CPU score of 135068.95. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 11548.62 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 532.33 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and cryptographic operations.

This instance is highly efficient for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads. It achieves top-tier results in database operations, Redis SET operations at 212.01 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput of 220.56 GB/sec. It is also well-suited for large language model prompt processing, though text generation speeds for smaller models scale at an average tier. The high density of dedicated cores makes it a strong fit for enterprise database hosting, heavy CI/CD compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a dedicated x86_64 server featuring 144 vCPUs (72 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor, paired with 540 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPUs, this instance excels in multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, achieving top-tier benchmarks in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations. It supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX), making it highly efficient for parallel processing tasks. This server is optimized for demanding workloads such as enterprise database hosting, static web serving, and large language model prompt processing.
